title: Passenger Side Register Removal and Installation
introduction:
The passenger side register is the dashboard air outlet assembly. Reaching it means working through the trim in layers: the side panel, the center upper panel, then the passenger finish panel. I think of it as unwrapping the dashboard sandwich—the outlet is inside, and the clips explain how each layer comes apart.

Use the drawings to locate the highlighted attachments before releasing each panel. This is an outlet removal and refit guide; it does not diagnose an airflow or temperature complaint.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Wear protective equipment
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during vehicle service. Use protective gloves when handling sharp or pointed parts; failure to use the specified protection may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Review applicable precautions
items.detail: Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) and [Climate Control System Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693184) before beginning.

items.name: Trim-removal tool
items.detail: Have the trim-removal tool depicted in the drawings ready to release the panel attachments at their highlighted locations.

items.name: Torque tool
items.detail: Use a torque tool capable of applying the passenger finish-panel retainer specification stated in the removal step when those retainers are reinstalled.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps before starting; they also contain details needed during installation.
edits.why: The finish-panel retainer torque appears during removal, so keep it available for reassembly.

edits.text: Use the depicted trim-removal tool to release the clips along the passenger end of the instrument panel, beside the glove compartment, then remove the instrument panel side trim panel.
edits.why: The drawing highlights the narrow side panel and its vertically arranged clips. I use those attachment locations to guide the tool rather than guessing where the panel is held.

edits.text: NOTE: The illustration shows a vehicle with center gauges; removal is similar on vehicles without center gauges.
edits.why: Match the trim and attachment layout while allowing for the different center-gauge configuration.

edits.text: Release the instrument panel center upper trim panel at the highlighted clips across its face, using the depicted trim-removal tool. As the panel comes free, disconnect its electrical connector and remove the panel.
edits.why: The drawing maps the clips across the center and passenger portions of the panel; its inset locates the electrical connection behind the center area. The panel is still electrically attached after its trim clips release.

edits.text:
Remove the threaded retainers beneath the passenger outlet end of the finish panel, then release the highlighted clips along the panel and remove the instrument panel passenger side finish panel. During installation, tighten the threaded retainers to the specified torque.
Torque: 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm)
edits.why: This panel has both threaded retainers and clips. Releasing only the clips leaves the outlet end fastened in place; the torque applies when the threaded retainers go back.

edits.text: With the passenger side finish panel removed, release the highlighted retaining clips around the register housing and separate the passenger side register assembly from the panel.
edits.why: The rear view exposes the register’s attachment to the finish panel. These clips retain the outlet assembly itself, after the surrounding dashboard trim has been removed.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence. Fit the register assembly into the passenger side finish panel and engage its clips. Refit the finish panel, engage its clips, and install its threaded retainers using the torque specified in the removal step. Reconnect the center upper trim panel electrical connector before seating that panel and engaging its clips. Finally, refit the instrument panel side trim panel and engage its clips.
edits.why: Working back through the layers restores the outlet attachment first and the outer trim last. I check each set of clips as its panel seats, keeping the electrical reconnection ahead of closing the center upper panel.

editorialRevision.scope: Only first preparation detail changed. Full source, all four original technical figures, final prose and verdict read; mechanical steps and2.5Nm preserved.
